situation: Imagine that a research firm is doing a telephone survey of people in your city You have agreed to answer some questions about sports.

questions.transcript: What sports do you enjoy playing?
How often do you usually play sports?
Do you think it is important for children to play sports? Why or why not?

situation: Imagine that a British marketing firm is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about how you use your vacation time.

questions.transcript: If you could take a vacation next week, where would you go?
How long do you usually spend on vacation, and who do you go with?
When you go on vacation, do you plan your time thoroughly or do you go without many plans? Describe your style of traveling.

situation: Imagine that an American marketing firm is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about bookstores.

questions.transcript: How many books do you read a month, and where do you usually buy them?
How often do you visit bookstores, and what do you usually do there?
How do you think bookstores can improve their services?

situation: Imagine that a Canadian marketing firm is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about local restaurants.

questions.transcript: What is your favorite local restaurant and how often do you eat there?
How much do you usually spend on a meal at a local restaurant?
How would your habits of eating out change if restaurants became more expensive?

situation: Imagine that an American marketing firm is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about shopping for clothing.

questions.transcript: How often do you shop for new clothing and who do you usually go with?
What aspect of clothes shopping do you find most pleasant?
Do you prefer shopping for clothing at a store or online and why?

situation: Imagine that a British marketing firm is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about cell phones.

questions.transcript: How much did you pay for your cell phone, and how old is it?
What's the most important feature you look at when you choose a new cell phone?
What do you like or dislike about using your cell phone and why?

situation: Imagine that a Canadian company is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about movies.

questions.transcript: How often do you go to the movie theater?
What is your favorite movie genre?
What are the advantages of watching movies at home?

situation: Imagine that a US marketing firm is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about watching television.

questions.transcript: How often do you watch television and where do you watch television?
What are your favorite television programs?
Do you watch television less or more than you used to in the past?

situation: Imagine that a Canadian marketing firm is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about pets.

questions.transcript: What kind of pet do you want to have if you don't have one now?
What is the main reason for having a pet?
What are the facts that people have to consider thinking about when having a pet?

situation: Imagine that a Canadian marketing company is doing research in your country. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about telephones.

questions.transcript: How often do you use a pay phone and when was the last time you used it?
Do you have a cellular phone? Then, how much do you usually spend on your monthly bill?
In what situations should people be careful when they talk on a phone?

situation: Imagine that a Canadian marketing firm is doing research in your area. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about amusement parks that have attractions like roller coasters.

questions.transcript: How often do you visit an amusement park, and who do you usually go there with?
What time of the day is best for visiting an amusement park? Why?
What could amusement parks in your city do to increase the number of visitors?

situation: Imagine that a British fitness magazine is preparing an article on exercise habits. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about walking.

questions.transcript: How often do you walk for exercise?
If you wanted to go for a walk, where would you go, and why?
People exercise in many different ways. What are some advantages of choosing walking instead of other forms of exercise?

situation: Imagine that your friend is planning to go shopping. You and your friend are having a telephone conversation about shopping for clothes.

questions.transcript: Do you usually buy clothes before traveling? Why?
What kind of clothes do people in your town usually wear these days?
Please explain a good place to buy clothes in your city and why.

situation: Imagine that a local press is doing research in your country to collect information for an article. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about conversation.

questions.transcript: When you meet your friends, what do you normally talk about?
Where do you usually go when you and your friends want to have a conversation?
Who is your favorite person to have a conversation with? Why?

situation: Imagine that an Australian marketing firm is doing research in your area. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about a town you want to live in.

questions.transcript: Which town do you live in, and how long have you been living there?
Do you have a plan to move out in the near future? Why or why not?
What are the important things you would consider when moving to a new place?

situation: Imagine that a British F&B brand is doing a research in your country. you have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about eating.

questions.transcript: What is your favorite food?
How often do you eat in a day?
Describe the typical meal you would have for dinner.

situation: A fitness center is doing a research in your area. You have agreed to participate in an interview about exercise.

questions.transcript: Do you work out regularly? Why do you exercise?
What else do you do other than exercise?
Can you describe your favorite exercise.

situation: Imagine that a friend is in your town for a few days. You’re having a phone conversation about places to go to.

questions.transcript: What’s a good place to visit in your area, and how far is it from the bus station?
It sounds like an interesting place. What are some things I can do there?
If I want to buy some gifts and souvenirs, where would you suggest I go?

situation: Imagine that a friend will be moving to your neighborhood. You are having a telephone conversation about where you live.

questions.transcript: How many grocery stores are in your neighborhood, and can you walk to them?
What’s the best time of day to go to the grocery store, and why?
Do you usually buy all your groceries from the same store? Why or why not?

situation: Imagine that an English-language technology magazine is doing research in your area. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about mobile applications, or apps. Apps are computer programs designed to be used on devices like tablets or mobile phones.

questions.transcript: Do you use mobile apps regularly? Why or why not?
If you wanted to purchase an app, would you be more likely to buy an app for learning or for entertainment? Why?
If you wanted to purchase an app, which of the following would most influence your decision? Why?

questions.transcript: When was the last time you were on vacation?
Do you usually travel alone or in a group?
